node.title: Principles of Inheritance and Variation: Mendel’s law of inheritance: Inheritance of one

questions.stem: The genotypic ratio in the F2 generation of a monohybrid cross is
questions.explanation: Selfing the heterozygous F1 (Tt) gives F2 progeny in the proportion 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt, so the genotypic ratio is 1 : 2 : 1. Because TT and Tt look alike under complete dominance, the phenotypic ratio is 3 : 1.

optionRationale.2: 3 : 1 is the phenotypic ratio under complete dominance, not the genotypic ratio.
optionRationale.3: 1 : 1 is the ratio of a test cross of a heterozygote.
optionRationale.4: 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 is the phenotypic ratio of a dihybrid cross.

questions.objective: State the genotypic ratio of a monohybrid F2

questions.stem: The chromosomal theory of inheritance was proposed independently by
questions.explanation: Walter Sutton and Theodor Boveri independently noted in 1902 that the behaviour of chromosomes during meiosis parallels that of Mendel's factors. They proposed that chromosomes carry the hereditary factors, which is the chromosomal theory of inheritance.

optionRationale.1: Watson and Crick proposed the double helix model of DNA.
optionRationale.3: Hershey and Chase showed that DNA is the genetic material of bacteriophage.
optionRationale.4: Meselson and Stahl showed that DNA replication is semi-conservative.

questions.objective: Recall the proposers of the chromosomal theory

questions.stem: The sex chromosome constitution of a person with Klinefelter's syndrome is
questions.explanation: Klinefelter's syndrome is caused by an extra X chromosome in a male, giving the karyotype 44 autosomes plus XXY, a total of 47 chromosomes. Such males are sterile with some feminine development such as breast development (gynaecomastia). Turner's syndrome is the XO condition.

optionRationale.1: XO (45 chromosomes) is Turner's syndrome in females.
optionRationale.2: XYY is not the Klinefelter karyotype; Klinefelter males have two X chromosomes.
optionRationale.4: XX is the normal female constitution.

questions.objective: State the karyotype of Klinefelter's syndrome

questions.stem: Haemophilia, a sex-linked recessive disorder, is a defect in
questions.explanation: In haemophilia a protein that is a part of the cascade of reactions leading to blood clotting is affected, so a simple cut can result in non-stop bleeding. The gene is on the X chromosome and is recessive, so the disease is more common in males than in females.

optionRationale.1: Defective haemoglobin chain synthesis is seen in sickle-cell anaemia and thalassemia.
optionRationale.2: Defective colour vision is colour blindness, a different X-linked disorder.
optionRationale.3: Lack of phenylalanine hydroxylase causes phenylketonuria.

questions.stem: Phenylketonuria is caused by the lack of the enzyme that converts the amino acid phenylalanine into
questions.explanation: Phenylketonuria is an autosomal recessive inborn error of metabolism. The enzyme phenylalanine hydroxylase is missing, so phenylalanine cannot be changed into tyrosine and instead accumulates and is converted into phenylpyruvic acid, which affects the brain and causes mental retardation.

optionRationale.1: Tryptophan is another amino acid and is not the product of this reaction.
optionRationale.3: Alanine is not formed from phenylalanine by this enzyme.
optionRationale.4: Glycine is not formed from phenylalanine by this enzyme.

questions.objective: Explain the metabolic block in phenylketonuria

questions.stem: Pleiotropy is the phenomenon in which
options: many genes together control a single trait
both alleles of a gene are fully expressed in the heterozygote
one allele is partly dominant over the other
one gene has several phenotypic effects
questions.explanation: In pleiotropy a single gene produces more than one phenotypic effect, as in phenylketonuria, where the mutant gene causes mental retardation and also reduced hair and skin pigmentation. Polygenic inheritance, co-dominance and incomplete dominance are the other situations named in the options.

optionRationale.1: Many genes controlling one trait is polygenic inheritance.
optionRationale.2: Full expression of both alleles in the heterozygote is co-dominance.
optionRationale.3: One allele being partly dominant is incomplete dominance.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about the ABO blood group system.
A. A person carries at most two of the three alleles of the I gene.
B. The alleles IA and IB are co-dominant.
C. The allele i is recessive and does not produce any sugar.
D. A person of blood group O has the genotype IA IB.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: The I gene has three alleles but every person is diploid and carries only two of them, so A is correct. IA and IB both express their sugars when together, so they are co-dominant (B). The allele i produces no sugar and is recessive (C). Group O is genotype ii, so D is wrong.

optionRationale.1: Statement C is also correct, so this is incomplete.
optionRationale.2: Statement A is also correct, so this is incomplete.
optionRationale.4: Statement D is false; IA IB gives group AB, and group O is ii.

questions.objective: Evaluate statements on multiple alleles and blood groups

questions.stem: Match List-I (cross) with List-II (phenotypic ratio in the progeny) and choose the correct code.

left: A. Dihybrid F2 with independent assortment
B. Test cross of a monohybrid heterozygote
C. F2 of a monohybrid cross with incomplete dominance
D. F2 of a monohybrid cross with complete dominance

questions.explanation: A dihybrid F2 gives 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 (A-I). A test cross of a heterozygote gives 1 : 1 (B-II). With incomplete dominance the phenotypic ratio follows the genotypic ratio, 1 : 2 : 1 (C-III), while complete dominance gives 3 : 1 (D-IV).

optionRationale.2: A and D are interchanged; 3 : 1 is a monohybrid ratio and 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 a dihybrid ratio.
optionRationale.3: B and C are interchanged; the test cross gives 1 : 1.
optionRationale.4: A and C are interchanged; the dihybrid ratio is 9 : 3 : 3 : 1.

questions.objective: Match crosses with their phenotypic ratios

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Genes that lie close together on a chromosome show a low frequency of recombination.
Reason (R): Morgan worked on Drosophila melanogaster and studied linkage in it.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: The closer two genes are, the less likely a crossover falls between them, so their recombination frequency is low. Morgan did use Drosophila to study linkage, so R is true, but the choice of organism does not explain why nearby genes recombine rarely.

optionRationale.1: The choice of Drosophila by Morgan is historical and does not explain the low recombination of close genes.
optionRationale.3: R is true; Morgan used Drosophila melanogaster for his linkage work.
optionRationale.4: A is true; tightly linked genes show less recombination.

questions.objective: Relate gene distance to recombination frequency

questions.stem: A dihybrid RrYy plant is test crossed with rryy. Assuming independent assortment, the fraction of the progeny expected to be rryy is
questions.explanation: The RrYy parent forms four types of gametes RY, Ry, rY and ry in equal proportion, while the rryy parent forms only ry. The progeny are therefore RrYy, Rryy, rrYy and rryy in the ratio 1 : 1 : 1 : 1, so rryy forms one quarter.

optionRationale.1: 1/16 would be the fraction if both parents were dihybrid and only one of 16 combinations were considered.
optionRationale.2: 1/2 would be the figure for a single-gene test cross, not a dihybrid one.
optionRationale.4: 3/16 is the fraction of one of the two 3-class phenotypes in a dihybrid F2.

questions.objective: Compute progeny of a dihybrid test cross

questions.stem: Two linked genes show 12 per cent recombination. In a test cross that gives 2500 progeny, the number of parental-type individuals expected is
questions.explanation: The recombination frequency of 12 per cent means that 12 per cent of the progeny are recombinant. The recombinants are 0.12 x 2500 = 300, so the parental types are the rest: 2500 - 300 = 2200, which is 88 per cent of the progeny.

optionRationale.1: 300 is the number of recombinants, not parental types.
optionRationale.2: 1250 is half of the progeny and corresponds to 50 per cent recombination, which would be free assortment.
optionRationale.3: 1100 is half of the parental total, counting only one parental class.

questions.objective: Calculate parental types from recombination frequency

questions.stem: A pedigree shows two unaffected parents who have an affected daughter. The trait is most likely
questions.explanation: Unaffected parents with an affected child means the trait is recessive, as a dominant trait cannot skip. An affected daughter would need to inherit the allele from her father, who is unaffected, so X-linked recessive is ruled out. The trait is autosomal recessive with both parents carriers.

optionRationale.2: A daughter with an X-linked recessive disorder must have an affected father, but he is unaffected.
optionRationale.3: A dominant trait cannot appear in a child if neither parent shows it.
optionRationale.4: A Y-linked trait passes only from father to son, so it cannot affect a daughter.

questions.objective: Deduce the mode of inheritance from a pedigree

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about X-linked recessive inheritance, such as haemophilia.
A. An affected father cannot pass the allele to his son.
B. A carrier mother can pass the allele to both sons and daughters.
C. All daughters of an affected father and a normal homozygous mother are carriers.
D. An affected daughter can be born to a carrier mother and a normal father.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: A father gives his Y chromosome to his sons, so he cannot pass the X-linked allele to them (A). A carrier mother can pass the allele to sons and daughters (B). Daughters of an affected father receive his X and are carriers if the mother is homozygous normal (C). An affected daughter needs an affected father, so D is wrong.

optionRationale.1: Statement C is also correct, so this misses it.
optionRationale.3: Statement D is false, and statement A is left out.
optionRationale.4: Statement D is false, and statement B is left out.

questions.objective: Evaluate statements on X-linked recessive inheritance

questions.stem: A couple plans to have three children. The probability that exactly two are daughters and one is a son is
questions.explanation: Each child is a daughter or a son with probability 1/2 independently. There are three ways in which one son can be placed among three births, and each specific order has a probability of 1/2 x 1/2 x 1/2 = 1/8. The probability is 3 x 1/8 = 3/8.

optionRationale.1: 1/8 is the probability of one specific order, such as daughter, daughter, son, and not of all three orders.
optionRationale.2: 1/4 is not the result of counting three possible orders with probability 1/8 each.
optionRationale.4: 1/2 would need four of the eight equally likely outcomes, but only three give two daughters.

questions.objective: Apply the rule of addition and multiplication to sex of children

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): A child with blood group O can be born to parents of blood groups A and B.
Reason (R): The parents may be heterozygous, with genotypes $I^A i$ and $I^B i$, and each can pass on the allele i.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: If the group A parent is $I^A i$ and the group B parent is $I^B i$, each forms gametes carrying i with a probability of one half. A child receiving i from both parents has the genotype ii and blood group O, so the heterozygous genotypes in R explain A.

optionRationale.2: R is the direct genetic reason for A, not just a related fact.
optionRationale.3: R is true; heterozygous parents can each pass on the recessive allele i.
optionRationale.4: A is true; group O children can arise from group A and group B parents.

questions.objective: Explain inheritance of group O from A and B parents
